as was the body of the 356, the work of Porsche employee Erwin Komenda, while some mechanical components, including the engine block and some suspension components, were based on and initially purchased from Volkswagen. The 356 was a luxury sports car and Porsche's first production automobile. Engineering innovations continued throughout the production years, contributing to its sporting successes and popularity. Production began in 1948 in Gmünd, Austria, where around 50 cars were built. On June 8, 1948, the first Porsche car obtained the relevant homologation: it was the Porsche 356/1 Roadster followed by the 356/2 until 1950. In 1950 the factory was moved to Zuffenhausen, Germany, and here are the first 356 also called, retrospectively, "Pre-A". Initially only 1100 cc, then 1300 cc and from 1952 also 1500 cc were easily recognizable by the windshield divided into two parts by a central rib. All were also available in a convertible version (Cabriolet, Speedster and then Roadster).

The 356 1500 cc, so-called "Pre A", produced between 1953 and 1955 is distinguished from the previous one by a series of characteristics. The bumpers are separated from the bodywork. the windshield is now in one piece with a curve in the center (Knickscheibe). The handle on the luggage compartment lid is elongated and has a slot, from 1954 with a Porsche emblem. The rear lights become round. The rear turn signals, also round, are close to the rear lights. The front turn signals are round and flat, from 1954 integrated into the horn grille. The brake light is integrated into the rear light cluster. The license plate lighting is in a chrome housing above the license plate. The engine is of the type 546/2, longitudinal rear, 4-cylinder boxer, air-cooled, has a displacement of 1,488 cc and is fed by two Solex 32 PBI carburetors. The distribution is single overhead camshaft with pushrods and rocker arms and valves. The compression of 7:1 for a power of 55 hp at 4,400 rpm, while the 1500S, the top-of-the-range engine has 70 hp. The chassis is a platform, the suspension is with longitudinal wishbones and transverse torsion bars. Rear axles with swing axles with longitudinal arms. Steering is with screw and roller. Drum brakes. The traction, obviously, is rear. The clutch is a single dry plate and the gearbox (type 519) is mechanical with 4 gears. The weight is about 830 kg, for a length of just under 4m.
In 1956 the 356 was replaced by the 356 A. General production of the 356 continued until April 1965, well after the new 911 model had made its debut in the autumn of 1963.
It appears that 76,313 units were produced. Of these, 7627 between the (about 50) “Gmünd” and the “Pre-A”
